themes_detail.label: Street sweeping collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street Sweeping complaints spiked to 19 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.9 per week (913% increase, z-score 9.01), signaling a potential sanitation service failure or sudden contractor issue affecting Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights residents.
evidence: 19 street sweeping complaints THIS WEEK vs 1.9 weekly baseline (913% spike)
Z-score of 9.01 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Concurrent spike in litter basket requests (13 complaints last week vs 1.4 avg, +846%) suggests sanitation infrastructure strain
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation to determine if there's a staffing shortage, route change, or equipment failure in CD 302
Canvass Fort Greene and Brooklyn Heights block captains to document street cleanliness patterns and identify which neighborhoods are most affected

themes_detail.label: Tree damage surge
themes_detail.summary: Damaged Tree complaints exploded to 18 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 2.1 per week (747% increase, z-score 8.08), potentially indicating storm damage, disease outbreak, or borough-wide infrastructure issue requiring immediate Parks investigation.
evidence: 18 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK vs 2.1 weekly average (747% spike)
Z-score of 8.08 represents extreme statistical anomaly
Recent local news mentions of fire/blaze in Brooklyn Heights (2026-03-13) may indicate related infrastructure damage
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent storm, fire, or construction activity caused the damage spike—obtain Parks Dept incident logs
Document specific tree locations and types of damage (broken limbs, disease, uprooting) to determine if there's a common cause
Interview arborists and residents about public safety risks from damaged trees in high-density neighborhoods

themes_detail.label: Street noise complaint surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints jumped to 54 THIS WEEK versus 14.4 weekly average (276% increase, z-score 7.46), representing the sharpest spike in exterior noise complaints and suggesting construction, event activity, or vehicle traffic escalation.
evidence: 54 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs 14.4 weekly baseline (276% increase)
Z-score of 7.46 indicates statistically extreme spike
1004 active DOB permits filed in last 90 days (753 alterations) suggest heavy construction activity that may correlate with noise
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 noise complaints with DOB alteration permits to identify which construction projects are generating complaints
Contact NYPD and 311 to determine if there are specific locations (e.g., Flatbush Ave, St. Felix) driving the spike
Interview residents about sleep disruption and enforcement gaps; compare response times for noise violations

themes_detail.label: Street condition deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street Condition complaints surged to 69 THIS WEEK from a 20.0 weekly average (245% increase, z-score 5.39), coinciding with high snow/ice complaints (1024 over 90 days) and suggesting deferred pothole repairs or salt damage compounding winter wear.
evidence: 69 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs 20.0 weekly average (245% spike)
Z-score of 5.39 represents significant statistical anomaly
1024 snow/ice complaints over 90-day period suggests ongoing winter damage; street condition spike may indicate post-winter assessment of damage
reporting_angles: Request DOT data on pothole repair backlogs and response times in CD 302; determine if there's a maintenance staffing shortage
Photograph worst streets (especially in Fort Greene where complaints may concentrate) and document hazards for cyclists and pedestrians
Interview residents and businesses about accident claims and vehicle damage related to poor street conditions

themes_detail.label: Sewer system stress
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints jumped to 19 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 3.6 per week (424% increase, z-score 9.75), potentially signaling blockages, overflow, or aging infrastructure failure that may require DEP investigation and could threaten public health.
evidence: 19 sewer complaints LAST WEEK vs 3.6 weekly average (424% spike)
Z-score of 9.75 represents most extreme statistical anomaly in dataset
Concurrent spike in plumbing complaints (288 total over 90 days, #10 category) suggests resident-side backups tied to system failure
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DEP to determine if there were sewer blockages, overflows, or failures in CD 302 last week—obtain incident reports
Interview plumbers operating in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights about surge in basement backups or drainage complaints
Investigate whether aging infrastructure in these historic neighborhoods is driving recurring sewer issues; tie to CB budget requests for DEP upgrades
